tasks.short: I enter invoices and receipts in AFAS and keep the AP and AR records current.

today.trigger: An invoice, credit note or bank transaction arrives.
steps: Collect invoices from Outlook and agency portals, and transactions from Rabobank.
Find the supplier or customer in AFAS and check supporting documents.
Enter or correct amounts, references and site allocations.
Post the transaction and attach its evidence.
Check that it appears correctly in the ledger and open items.
drudgery: Downloading and attaching the same documents
today.time_sinks: Missing references, inconsistent agency files and repeated entry between portals and AFAS.

lenses.faster: Import structured invoices and bank files directly, eliminating retyping and routine attachment work. Put incomplete records in one exception queue.
lenses.autonomous: A received invoice or bank file starts validation and matching. Approved structured matches post automatically; PDF proposals and uncertain matches wait for review.
lenses.ambitious: Keep AP and AR current throughout the day across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Give the close team a daily view of missing transactions and unresolved items.
lenses.joy: Remove field copying and repeated screen checks. Leave supplier problem solving and fixing recurring causes of exceptions.
lenses.options: For an uncertain record, show possible existing suppliers or matching documents with supporting references. Never create a supplier or select an IBAN from a model guess.
lenses.altitude: I own the intake rules, supplier data quality and exception queue rather than keying every record.
reach: Accountant: prepare evidence for AP and AR close reconciliations
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: specify finance import checks
Controller: report posting delays and their causes

tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a plausible transaction does not reflect what Noordhaven actually bought or received.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured imports, matching and posting use checkable rules. PDF extraction is a separate llm_step or existing capture service, with review before uncertain records post.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice enters the finance mailbox or an authorised portal or bank import completes.
steps: Register the source document and a unique processing identifier.
Import UBL and structured files; extract PDF fields into a proposal.
Validate totals, supplier identity, duplicates and available order or receipt matches.
Post only records that meet approved deterministic rules; queue all other proposals.
Record posting results and reconcile intake totals to AFAS.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper reviews PDF proposals and exceptions; authorised owners approve supplier changes and rule changes. Bank release remains a separate approval.
systems: Staffing agency portals or authorised exports
data_needed: Approved posting rules and site codes
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS document and posting history, plus a proposed restricted SharePoint import register containing source IDs, rule versions and exceptions.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports PDF invoice capture, with manual completion and booking where needed.
An AFAS partner describes Profit 8 posting and approving one-to-one invoice matches; Noordhaven's version and configuration remain unverified.
Escalante Golf reportedly reduced invoice processing from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds in NetSuite; this does not establish Noordhaven's result.

risks: Noordhaven may lack the AFAS version, configuration or receipt records needed for automatic posting.
Retries could create duplicate transactions without unique identifiers and reconciliation.
PDF content could contain misleading instructions; extraction must treat it only as data.
Agency invoices may contain personal data that should not enter unrestricted model services.
research_questions: Which AFAS version and invoice-processing features are enabled?
What proportion of invoices have UBL and reliable order or receipt references?
Can all three agency portals provide stable authorised exports?
Does a representative pilot reduce total handling time without increasing incorrect postings?

tasks.short: I check invoice totals, postings, VAT codes and site allocations before errors reach the close.

today.trigger: A posting proposal, invoice batch or reconciliation needs checking.
steps: Open the document and its AFAS entry.
Recalculate totals and compare quantities, rates and VAT.
Check ledger codes, site allocations and accounting dates.
Compare agency invoices with approved hours and agreed rates.
Correct mistakes or ask the responsible person for clarification.
drudgery: Comparing long agency invoice lists line by line
today.time_sinks: Finding approved hours and rate agreements, then separating genuine differences from rounding or timing differences.

lenses.faster: Run arithmetic, duplicate, period and permitted-code checks on every record. Show only failed checks with the relevant document lines.
lenses.autonomous: Each import or posting proposal triggers the checks. Clean records pass the validation stage; failed records remain blocked for resolution.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice against approved hours and effective rates, including agreed shift premiums. Detect recurring errors before they distort site costs and forecasts.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive recalculation. Keep the investigation of unusual charges and conversations that prevent repeat errors.
lenses.options: Show whether a difference comes from hours, rates, premiums, VAT or rounding. Offer evidence-backed correction proposals without changing the source records.
lenses.altitude: I maintain the control rules and review where they fail, rather than inspect every correct line.
reach: Controller: maintain AP control evidence and exception trends
Payroll Specialist: flag differences between billed agency premiums and approved rate schedules
Accountant: prepare correction proposals with supporting documents

tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a legitimate commercial exception from a mistake, especially when operational records disagree.
tasks.pattern_why: Arithmetic, valid codes, effective dates and invoice-to-hours comparisons can be explicit rules. A model may explain a failure but cannot establish the correct amount.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice proposal or new posting enters the validation queue.
steps: Read the document fields, posting proposal and supporting records.
Apply versioned arithmetic, duplicate, VAT-code and period checks.
Match agency lines to approved hours and effective contractual rates.
Pass clean records and route failures with quantified differences.
Record the resolution and propose recurring control improvements.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper resolves exceptions; the Accountant approves unusual VAT treatment and material corrections. HR or Payroll confirms CAO-related rate interpretation.
data_needed: Approved hours by agency, site and period
in_practice.logs_to: A proposed control register linked to AFAS documents, recording each check, rule version, failure, reviewer and resolution.

evidence.claim: Profit 8 supports one-to-one invoice matching according to an AFAS partner.
Checking agency invoice hours and effective rates with deterministic comparisons is feasible, but Noordhaven's required joins are unproven.

risks: Incorrect rate schedules make consistent errors look correct.
Approved hours may arrive late or use different worker and period identifiers.
Broad tolerances could hide systematic overbilling.
Worker-level data requires restricted access under AVG/GDPR; medical absence details are unnecessary.
research_questions: Can agency invoice lines be joined reliably to approved hours?
Who owns effective rates and interpretation of applicable CAO premiums?
Which historical errors would the proposed checks detect or miss?
How many false exceptions appear when testing a full seasonal billing cycle?

tasks.short: I give invoices the right ledger account, VAT code and Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo cost centre.

today.trigger: An invoice or credit note needs accounting codes.
steps: Read the invoice and identify the purchase purpose.
Check similar supplier postings and the coding guidance.
Select the ledger account, VAT code and site allocation.
Ask the budget owner about unclear or shared costs.
Save the coding and supporting explanation in AFAS.
today.time_sinks: Mixed invoices, missing site references and purchases whose accounting treatment differs from previous supplier invoices.

lenses.faster: Apply approved mappings to recurring structured lines and prefill the rest. Show the source text and coding rule beside each proposal.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice intake triggers coding proposals. Exact approved mappings can run unattended; model-derived codes require approval before posting.
lenses.ambitious: Code at line level so site costs and agency charges are visible consistently. Reduce the recoding work that delays a trusted forecast.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated searches through old postings. Keep interpreting unusual purchases and improving coding guidance.
lenses.options: For ambiguous descriptions, show up to three permitted codes and explain the evidence for each. Ask for missing purchase purpose rather than invent it.
lenses.altitude: I own a tested coding catalogue and review how coding quality changes over time.
reach: Controller: improve cost-centre discipline
FP&A Analyst: prepare consistent site cost classifications
Accountant: identify purchases needing capitalisation review

tasks.human_edge: Understanding purchase purpose and recognising when historical treatment was wrong or no longer applies.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured invoice descriptions become constrained coding proposals within a deterministic workflow. Exact mappings need no model, while ambiguous coding stays subject to review.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice has captured fields but lacks approved accounting codes.
steps: Load the invoice lines and permitted coding catalogue.
Apply exact approved mappings where available.
Generate proposals for remaining lines using source text and reviewed examples.
Reject invalid combinations and flag tax, capitalisation or allocation uncertainty.
Present proposals for approval and record corrections for catalogue review.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves each model-derived proposal. The Accountant decides unusual VAT or capitalisation treatment; budget owners confirm uncertain site splits.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and VAT codes
Purchase purpose and approved allocation rules
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS posting evidence and a proposed restricted coding register with source lines, proposed codes, model version, approval and final codes.

evidence.claim: Zone & Co describes coding suggestions from vendor history with team review and confirmation.
Constrained coding proposals using Noordhaven's catalogue are plausible; reliable AFAS integration and accuracy require a pilot.

risks: Supplier history can reproduce incorrect VAT or ledger treatment.
A confident proposal may hide missing purchase context.
Mixed invoices may need several codes and allocations.
Unreviewed corrections could contaminate future examples.
research_questions: What share of invoice lines have stable approved coding mappings?
How accurate are proposals on held-out invoices from all three sites?
Does reviewing proposals take less time than coding from scratch?
Which categories should always require Accountant review?

tasks.short: I calculate invoice balances, discounts and interest, and check amounts before we charge or pay them.

today.trigger: An invoice, settlement, overdue account or loan schedule needs an amount calculated.
steps: Find the original amount, relevant dates and agreed terms.
Check receipts, credits and previous charges in AFAS.
Calculate the balance, discount or interest in AFAS or Excel.
Check rounding, rate dates and any contractual exceptions.
Record the calculation for review or use in billing and payment preparation.
today.time_sinks: Finding the applicable terms and handling partial payments or rate changes.

lenses.faster: Use tested formulas fed by current AFAS balances and approved terms. Remove manual copying, arithmetic and repeated spreadsheet construction.
lenses.autonomous: A balance or approved terms change recalculates the amount and its supporting schedule. Missing terms or disputed balances stop the calculation from being used.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain daily calculations for all relevant open items. Give FP&A clearer estimates of receipts, discounts and financing costs.
lenses.joy: Remove calculator work and formula checking. Keep resolving why the amount differs from the customer's or supplier's expectation.
lenses.options: Compare payment on the due date, early payment with an eligible discount and later payment with applicable interest. Show assumptions and cash effects separately.
lenses.altitude: I maintain reliable calculation rules and exception handling instead of calculating each amount.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: prepare interest and settlement calculations
FP&A Analyst: prepare payment-date scenarios
Accountant: reconcile loan interest and principal schedules

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a charge or concession is commercially appropriate and whether the underlying terms are applicable.
tasks.pattern_why: Balances, interest, discounts and principal schedules use explicit formulas and approved inputs. A language model is unnecessary for arithmetic.

in_practice.trigger: An open-item balance changes or a scheduled daily calculation runs.
steps: Read current balances, receipt allocations and approved terms.
Select the effective formula and rate version.
Calculate amounts using defined date, rounding and currency rules.
Check results against control totals and flag missing or conflicting inputs.
Publish the calculation and permitted scenarios with an input timestamp.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves formulas and rate updates. Collections approves discretionary charges or concessions; payment and invoice release follow their own approval rules.
data_needed: Current open balances and allocated receipts
Approved interest rates with effective dates
in_practice.logs_to: A proposed calculation register linked to AFAS, storing input snapshots, formula versions, effective rates and results.

evidence.claim: Deterministic software can calculate balances, discounts and interest from explicit terms and dated inputs.
Dutch payment-term rules include a maximum of 30 days for large-company payments to SMEs; legal applicability must be confirmed.

risks: Wrong rate dates or day-count conventions produce precise but incorrect results.
Unallocated receipts overstate balances and interest.
Nightly Power BI data is too old for some same-day calculations.
Correct arithmetic does not establish the right to charge interest.
research_questions: Which calculations are still done outside AFAS, and why?
Are terms and rate changes available as approved structured data?
Do proposed formulas reproduce independently checked historical calculations?
How much elapsed time comes from finding terms rather than doing arithmetic?

tasks.short: I prepare Rabobank payment batches for suppliers, utilities and taxes, including agency g-rekening splits.

today.trigger: A scheduled payment run or an urgent authorised payment is due.
steps: Select approved unpaid invoices and tax payment instructions.
Check due dates, holds, credits and beneficiary details.
Calculate agreed agency g-rekening splits where applicable.
Prepare the AFAS payment batch for Rabobank.
Obtain approval and reconcile executed payments.
drudgery: Rechecking the same approved invoice list
today.time_sinks: Unapproved invoices, changed bank details, missing agency evidence and waiting for authorised bank signers.

lenses.faster: Build the batch from approved AFAS items and validated beneficiary records. Automate due-date selection, duplicate checks and approved g-rekening calculations.
lenses.autonomous: The payment calendar produces a checked batch and approval pack. No funds leave Rabobank until the authorised signer approves.
lenses.ambitious: Prepare payment runs early enough to resolve blocked invoices before due dates. Give Finance a clear view of upcoming cash needs and agency payment splits.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated list preparation and approval chasing. Keep investigating payment risks and resolving blockers with suppliers.
lenses.options: Show compliant payment schedules with cash impact and eligible discounts. Do not offer delaying small suppliers beyond applicable legal terms as a cash-saving option.
lenses.altitude: I own payment readiness and control quality while authorised signers retain release responsibility.
reach: FP&A Analyst: prepare near-term payment forecasts
Controller: maintain evidence of payment controls
Accountant: track agency g-rekening payments and supporting records

tasks.human_edge: Assessing urgent payment requests and independently verifying beneficiary changes before money moves.
tasks.pattern_why: Batch selection, totals and approved splits follow explicit rules. Each payment run has an independent human release gate.

in_practice.trigger: The payment calendar reaches a run date or an authorised urgent request is registered.
steps: Select approved items using current AFAS payment status and due dates.
Check duplicates, holds, credits and independently verified beneficiary details.
Calculate approved agency splits and flag missing supporting evidence.
Generate the payment batch and a totals-based approval pack.
Obtain authorised Rabobank release and reconcile execution results.
in_practice.human_gate: An authorised signer approves every batch. Changed IBANs and name-check warnings require independent verification and recorded resolution before release.
data_needed: Agency payment-behaviour statements and required records
Payment holds, due dates and bank execution statuses
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS payment history, Rabobank authorisation evidence and a proposed restricted register of beneficiary checks, split calculations and batch approvals.

evidence.claim: AFAS bank matching recognises creditor payment batches and can post their bank return to payments in transit.
Qualifying g-rekening deposits can limit inlenersaansprakelijkheid for the deposited amount; a payment-behaviour statement alone is no guarantee.
An IBAN-name mismatch warning can be overridden by the payer, so the check does not itself prevent payment.

risks: Fraudulent bank-detail changes can bypass otherwise correct invoice controls.
No universal g-rekening percentage should be assumed.
Rabobank's name-check handling for Noordhaven's batch channel must be verified.
Approval waiting time may limit end-to-end speedup even when preparation is faster.
research_questions: How does Noordhaven's Rabobank batch channel handle verification-of-payee results?
Who independently verifies beneficiary changes and releases batches?
Are agency split methods and required evidence complete and approved?
How much run time is preparation versus waiting for invoice and bank approval?

tasks.short: I reconcile AFAS totals with Excel trackers and agency records and explain the differences.

today.trigger: A daily check or month-close reconciliation compares AFAS with a separate record.
steps: Export AFAS transactions for the relevant period.
Collect the corresponding Excel tracker or agency statement.
Align references, dates and amounts.
Compare records and totals, then investigate differences.
Record explanations and obtain approval for necessary corrections.
today.time_sinks: Different cut-off dates, missing transaction identifiers and trackers that mix estimates with actual postings.

lenses.faster: Compare aligned records automatically and preserve the totals check. Show missing, duplicated and changed rows instead of making me scan the whole export.
lenses.autonomous: A new export or close cut-off triggers the comparison. Clean reconciliations produce evidence; differences go to the named owner.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile daily so month-end differences are already understood. Retire duplicate trackers once their control purpose is covered reliably.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet sorting and visual row matching. Keep tracing the causes of differences and improving source records.
lenses.options: Show timing differences, missing postings, duplicate entries and amount differences separately. Suggest explanations only where source evidence supports them.
lenses.altitude: I design reconciliation coverage and cut-offs rather than compare printouts or spreadsheets manually.
reach: Accountant: prepare AP and AR reconciliation packs
Controller: maintain close readiness and control completion
FP&A Analyst: distinguish estimates from booked actuals

tasks.human_edge: Determining which source is authoritative and whether a difference is timing, an estimate or an accounting error.
tasks.pattern_why: Record matching and control totals use explicit keys and cut-offs. A model can draft explanations, but reconciliation status must follow evidence.

in_practice.trigger: Both source datasets are available for the same reconciliation period.
steps: Capture dated source snapshots and verify completeness.
Normalise identifiers, amounts and agreed cut-off rules.
Match records and independently compare control totals.
Create an exception list with source links and named owners.
Record resolutions and issue the reconciliation evidence pack.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper resolves differences; the Accountant approves material corrections and required close sign-off. The workflow never posts a balancing entry merely to make totals agree.
data_needed: Source control totals and correction history
in_practice.logs_to: A proposed SharePoint reconciliation register containing source versions, totals, unmatched records, resolutions and sign-off references.

evidence.claim: AFAS already performs rule-based bank reconciliation and routes unrecognised lines for manual processing; this proves bank matching, not arbitrary tracker reconciliation.
Automated comparison of AFAS extracts with versioned Excel and agency records is plausible if keys and cut-offs are reliable.

risks: Matching totals can conceal offsetting errors unless individual records are also checked.
Nightly Power BI extracts may represent a different cut-off from live AFAS.
Poor identifiers can produce false matches.
An incomplete export could be mistaken for a clean reconciliation.
research_questions: Which separate trackers exist, and what independent control does each provide?
Can both sources be captured at consistent cut-offs with completeness checks?
Do proposed matches detect known historical differences without false clearing?
Which trackers could be retired after the replacement control is proven?

tasks.short: I look up invoices, balances and payments in AFAS to answer suppliers, customers and colleagues.

today.trigger: A supplier, customer or colleague asks about an invoice, payment or account.
steps: Read the request and identify the account and requester.
Find the invoice and current account status in AFAS.
Check payment execution, credits, holds and relevant correspondence.
Explain the status and identify any next action.
Reply and refer disputes or unresolved blockers to their owner.
drudgery: Searching invoice numbers across mail and AFAS
today.time_sinks: Unclear requests, multiple invoices in one message and distinguishing a prepared payment from an executed payment.

lenses.faster: Retrieve the relevant AFAS records and draft a reply with source links. Remove repeated searches and copying while I check the answer.
lenses.autonomous: An incoming account question starts requester verification, lookup and drafting. Every external reply waits for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Give all three sites consistent answers and track recurring questions. Fix avoidable payment-status queries by improving invoice references and status visibility.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive lookup and typing. Keep resolving difficult questions and maintaining supplier and customer trust.
lenses.options: Offer a short factual reply, a fuller explanation and a clarification request where identifiers are missing. Each version uses the same verified account facts.
lenses.altitude: I own answer quality, access rules and escalation paths instead of searching every account manually.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: prepare factual account-status responses
Accountant: assemble evidence for disputed postings
Controller: identify recurring approval and payment blockers

tasks.human_edge: Handling frustration, commercial sensitivity and disputes without making unsupported promises or disclosing another party's information.
tasks.pattern_why: The workflow interprets a request, checks identity, retrieves permitted records and drafts a response across systems. A person approves before communication counts.

in_practice.trigger: A message enters the AP or AR mailbox.
steps: Identify the request type, account reference and requester entitlement.
Retrieve only authorised current AFAS records and available bank execution evidence.
Distinguish proposed, approved, submitted and executed payments.
Draft a sourced reply or request clarification when facts are missing.
Present the draft for approval and record the approved response.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves every outgoing reply. Disputes, bank-detail requests and payment commitments go to the authorised owner.
systems: AFAS Profit through a proposed read-only connection
data_needed: Invoice identifiers and current open-item status
Approved response templates and escalation owners
in_practice.logs_to: A proposed restricted correspondence register linked to the Outlook conversation, with retrieved record IDs, timestamps, draft, reviewer and final reply.

evidence.claim: A read-only retrieval workflow can draft account-status replies from structured finance records, but this Noordhaven integration is unproven.
AFAS can clear recognised bank transactions automatically; reliable answers still require current records and confirmation of execution.

risks: A reply could reveal another customer's or supplier's account information.
The draft could describe a submitted batch as a completed payment.
Incoming email may contain malicious instructions and must be treated as untrusted content.
Human review may save little time if source retrieval is unreliable.
research_questions: What share of mailbox requests are simple status questions rather than disputes?
Can current AFAS and bank execution data be retrieved with restricted read-only access?
How will requester entitlement be verified?
Do reviewers approve pilot drafts faster without missing factual or disclosure errors?

tasks.short: I check overdue customer balances and scheduled loan payments and flag anything that needs action.

today.trigger: The daily ageing check runs or a scheduled loan payment approaches.
steps: Open the AFAS ageing report and approved loan schedules.
Check recent receipts, credits and bank transactions.
Identify overdue balances and missed or upcoming instalments.
Check disputes, holds and agreed payment arrangements.
Send the action list to Collections or the responsible finance owner.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same overdue action list
today.time_sinks: Unallocated receipts, outdated payment arrangements and repeated hand-offs about disputed balances.

lenses.faster: Combine current balances, matched receipts and payment schedules into a list of changes requiring action. Remove scans of accounts whose status has not changed.
lenses.autonomous: After bank matching, rules flag missed commitments, overdue balances and approaching instalments. Internal alerts go to the responsible owner automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Track every relevant payment commitment daily and expose emerging cash shortfalls earlier. Give Collections a cleaner queue that supports lower DSO.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated balance checking. Keep investigating missed payments and helping owners resolve blockers.
lenses.options: Show cash expectations assuming on-time payment, known delays and a conservative delay scenario. Label assumptions clearly rather than presenting predicted dates as commitments.
lenses.altitude: I maintain reliable account monitoring and ownership rules instead of checking every balance.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: maintain the factual collections queue
FP&A Analyst: prepare near-term receipt scenarios
Accountant: monitor scheduled loan-payment exceptions

tasks.human_edge: Understanding why payment is late and deciding when a sensitive account needs a conversation or escalation.
tasks.pattern_why: Due dates, payment commitments and receipt status support explicit monitoring rules. Negotiation, write-offs and formal collection action remain human decisions.

in_practice.trigger: Bank matching completes, a commitment changes or the daily monitoring schedule runs.
steps: Read current open items, unmatched receipts and approved repayment schedules.
Compare balances and dates with recorded commitments, disputes and holds.
Flag missed payments and upcoming obligations using approved thresholds.
Route changed exceptions to Collections or the relevant finance owner.
Refresh cash scenarios and record acknowledgement and resolution.
in_practice.human_gate: Collections decides customer contact, arrangements and escalation. The Accountant or Finance Director approves loan-related action; no automated renegotiation, write-off or payment release occurs.
systems: SharePoint or Excel approved loan schedules
Power BI for nightly trend reporting
data_needed: Current open items and matched receipts
Named account owners and alert thresholds
in_practice.logs_to: A proposed account-monitoring register linked to AFAS, recording source timestamps, rule versions, alerts, owners and resolutions.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches bank lines using references, account details and amounts, with exceptions handled manually.
Daily monitoring of due dates and recorded commitments is feasible with structured data; Noordhaven's schedule completeness is unverified.

risks: Unallocated receipts can trigger false overdue alerts.
Old disputes or payment commitments can make the action queue misleading.
Alert volume may overwhelm owners unless unchanged items are suppressed.
Loan covenant interpretation extends beyond routine payment monitoring.
research_questions: Are payment commitments and disputes recorded consistently in AFAS or another controlled register?
Who owns loan schedules, and is loan monitoring actually part of this role?
How many historical overdue alerts would disappear after correct receipt allocation?
Does the pilot reduce monitoring time and improve action ownership without duplicating Collections work?

role.altitude: The bookkeeper becomes the owner of reliable AP and AR flow: intake, coding rules, matching, exception resolution and evidence that the close team can trust.
reach: Accountant: prepare AP and AR close reconciliations and correction evidence
Controller: maintain transaction controls, exception trends and close readiness
Credit and Collections Officer: maintain account-status responses and a clean factual action queue
FP&A Analyst: prepare current payment and receipt inputs for cash forecasts
Payroll Specialist and HR: reconcile agency invoices against approved hours and contractual rate schedules
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks total 583.6 hours per FTE per year, about 36.5% of the supplied role baseline. Their boundaries may overlap, so savings must be measured once at workflow level. Today's steps are company-specific assumptions, not observations; all time savings and speedups are pilot estimates, not documented Noordhaven results. Speedups assume no additional queue delay and must be measured through completion, including approvals. Released hours create capacity, not automatic headcount or cash savings. Approval waits, missing receipts, agency data quality and commercial disputes limit the gains. Bank release, unusual accounting treatment, negotiations and statutory sign-off remain with authorised people.
skills_to_grow: Configure and test AFAS imports, matching rules and exception workflows
Maintain supplier data, coding catalogues and effective rate schedules
Use Excel Power Query and structured reconciliation methods
Design completeness checks, duplicate controls and audit evidence
Review model proposals against source documents
Apply restricted access and data minimisation under AVG/GDPR
Understand agency invoice controls and approved g-rekening arrangements
Measure touchless processing, error rates, queue age and close delays
role.ambitious_version: Across the three sites, the three bookkeepers run a daily AP and AR control queue in which approved structured transactions flow automatically and exceptions have clear owners. They provide the Accountant with reconciled close evidence, Collections with current balances and FP&A with traceable cash inputs. Success is more invoices processed without touch, fewer audit adjustments, lower DSO and fewer days to close with a forecast the business trusts. Start with existing AFAS capabilities and add model steps only where unstructured documents justify them. Keep CAO interpretation with HR and Payroll; these workflows need approved agency rates, not sickness or Wet verbetering poortwachter records. Involve the OR where the redesign changes working arrangements or introduces employee monitoring, and reassess EU AI Act obligations before extending administrative tools into employment decisions.
